evals.prompt: In this React app that uses Hearth, add a bill icon next to the 'Your bill' heading.
evals.expected_output: Runs `hearth icons search bill --json`, picks an icon from the result, runs `hearth icons get <name> --json` or uses the usage line, and imports it from the package the CLI reports.
expectations: Runs `hearth icons search` before writing the import
Passes --json and checks the exit code before using the output
Imports the icon from the package named in the CLI's usage, not from a guessed path
Does not use an icon name that the CLI did not return

evals.prompt: Make the helper text under this input use the secondary text colour. It's a web app styled with CSS modules.
evals.expected_output: Runs `hearth tokens search` for secondary text, prefers a semantic token, and uses its CSS variable in the CSS file with no hardcoded hex.
expectations: Looks the token up with `hearth tokens search` and `get` instead of guessing the variable
Uses a semantic token, not a primitive colour
Uses the css.variable value in the CSS file
Does not write a hex value

evals.prompt: In our Expo app, style this card background with the brand background colour and make sure it looks right in dark mode.
evals.expected_output: Runs `hearth tokens get semantic.background.brand --platform native --json` and uses the js path, which carries the dark value.
expectations: Passes --platform native explicitly
Uses the js path from the output rather than a CSS variable or a hex value
Does not take a dark value from a web (default platform) lookup

evals.prompt: Use the Hearth 'sparkle' icon on the rewards page.
evals.expected_output: Searches for the icon, finds no match (exit 1, total 0), tries a broader or synonym query at most once or twice, then tells the user no such icon exists instead of inventing a name.
expectations: Reads exit 1 from a search as no match, not as a failure to retry endlessly
Tries at most one or two other queries
Tells the user nothing fits and offers an alternative or a question
Does not import an icon name the CLI did not return

evals.prompt: Look up the token for the primary body text colour with the hearth CLI. (The CLI prints: Error [ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED]: Package subpath './hearth-manifest.json' is not defined by "exports" and exits 1 with nothing on stdout.)
evals.expected_output: Recognises the stack trace as a broken install, not a no-match, stops, tells the user, and does not retry or guess the token.
expectations: Does not treat exit 1 as a no-match
Does not retry the command or try variations
Tells the user the installed package hides its manifest and may be altered or not a Hearth release
Does not guess a token path from node_modules

evals.prompt: Find the Hearth logo to put in the footer. (The CLI exits 3 with: @utilitywarehouse/hearth-svg-assets is not installed in this project. Install it (npm install @utilitywarehouse/hearth-svg-assets) and run the command again.)
evals.expected_output: Relays the exit 3 message and the install command to the user and asks before installing.
expectations: Reports that the package is not installed and gives the command from the message
Does not run the install without asking
Does not invent a logo import path
